question.text: A light of energy <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>75</mn><mo> </mo><mi>eV</mi></math> is incident on a hydrogen atom in its ground state. The atom absorbs the radiation and reaches to one of its excited states. The angular momentum of the atom in the excited state is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mi>π</mi></mfrac><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>17</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>eVs</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ______ (use <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>14</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>eVs</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>8</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

solution.text:
Let the electron jumped to nth excited state.

In the ground state, energy E=-13.6 eV

So, using relation 12.75=13.6112-1n2

⇒0.9375=1-1n2⇒n2=16

⇒n=16=4

Now, angular momentum, L=nh2π=4h2π=2hπ

 =2π×4.14×10-15

=828×10-17π eVs

Hence, the value of x=828.
